_comment: which biases the recogniser toward these phrases without retraining anything. It costs no RAM,
no model and no time — the recogniser simply weights them higher when a sound is ambiguous.
DATA, NOT CODE, on purpose: main.swift reads this file every time it opens the microphone, so
adding a name takes an edit and no recompile. A rebuild to teach it one word is the kind of
friction that means the word never gets taught.
WHAT BELONGS HERE: proper nouns and terms the recogniser has no reason to know — people, brands,
places, dishes, the names of this system's own parts. NOT ordinary English. Apple's bias is
relative, so a list padded with common words dilutes the weight on the words that needed help.
Keep it to things that actually get mangled.
The cap is enforced in main.swift, not here — see the note beside contextualStrings.
PER USER. config/vocabulary.json is yours and is not committed; install.sh starts it from this file.
Add the names the recogniser mangles for YOU: your own name, family and friends, your town, the
shops and dishes you order — one phrase per entry. It is re-read every time the microphone opens.
